means: One folder holds one edition of a game's rules, in nine files.
A person or an agent reads it instead of the manual, and a program reads the same numbers from it.
Every number is written once.
All nine files must be there.
Each is one JSON object.
IDs start with a letter and use letters, digits and underscores, and an ID is used once in the folder; in `parts`, once in a group.
What a program computes from has named fields.
Everything else is `says`: words that are enough for a reader who never opens the manual.
Do not give structure to a rule that only people judge.
Every rule code has a record of its own, with its own `says`.
A number that a limit holds is named there, not typed.
If a rule is a whole list in `parts`, its `says` gives the rule and names the group.
A record may hold more values than are named here.
Use a name of letters, digits and underscores that says what it is, or add `of`.
A name that is nearly a known one of that kind of record is refused as a slip.
An extra value is a number, true or false, {"text": "words"}, or a list or group of them.
At the top of game.json, clock.json, field.json, scoring.json and robot.json only known names are allowed.
A place is both a target and a supply.
A piece put in one place often comes out of another.
Follow `takes`, `gives` and `then`, and no piece is lost or made.
A place that belongs to an alliance but stands at the other end is still written as blue's, where blue's stands.
A count belongs to the record of one alliance, all its spots together.
Do not type a count that the spots already make.
Examples here are invented.

In this file: `holds` is what a property holds (a form, or a list of words); `needs` names the fields that must be there; `one_of`, exactly one of these; `any_of`, at least one; `act_needs`, at least one of these when there is an `act`; `closed`, no extra values; `placed`, it may have the fields of `placed`; `geometry`, it needs geometry or `no_geometry` when a rule or score names it; `by_piece`, its fields are pieces' IDs; `optional`, a field of a shape that may be left out, where all others must be there; `as`, the form that an example is read as.
A name is nearly a known one when Python's difflib gives them a ratio of 0.85 or more.
A group with nothing in it may be left out.
A cost's `award` needs `to`. `instead_of` names a foul of the same list.
A pattern makes 1 to 1000 spots.
Only a state may have `my` or `their` in `when`.
A weight has one of the names given.

length.means: Lengths. A program gets them in mm.

mass.means: Masses. A program gets them in kg.

time.means: Times. A program gets them in s.

angle.means: Angles. A program gets them in degrees.

joined.means: Feet with inches, and minutes with seconds, may be joined: 5 ft 4 3/8 in.

kept.means: Units that are kept as printed. No others are allowed. A thicker wire has a smaller AWG, so use `thinnest`.

id.means: The name of a record: it starts with a letter and uses letters, digits and underscores. It is used once in the folder; in `parts`, once in a group.

path.means: The ID and then field names, with no file name. Some begin with a word instead (see `roots`). In a position, `stall.at.x` means the same alliance's stall; to name one from outside, write `stall@red`, and a spot after it. A list's parts are .x, .y and .z; a range's are .low and .high. A tolerance has .low and .high too. A path may end in the name of a variant, and goes on through `is` and `any`. A spot of a pattern is .1, .1.a or its name, after the ID and `.spots`, or after `@` and the alliance.

quantity.means: A number with its unit, as printed. Feet with inches, and minutes with seconds, may be joined.

tolerance.means: A number with a tolerance, in the same unit.

range.means: Both ends are printed. It has a low and a high, and no one number between.

limit.means: A limit on a quantity or a count.

any.means: One of these limits is enough.

formula.means: Worked out from other values: `=` and then paths, numbers and functions. Adding needs the same kind of number, and a bare number only multiplies or divides. An angle needs no conversion. A formula that names a value with variants has the same variants. If two values are equal because one is the other, write a formula. It gives a plain number: from a tolerance the number itself, and from a limit its number without the words.

by.means: A value that depends on a variant: `by` names the kind of variant, and each of its names has a value. One may hold another.

value.means: A printed value, or an object that says more about it.

extra.means: A value that is not named here: a number, true or false, or {"text": "words"}; or a list or group of them; or {"any": [...]} of which one is enough.

number.means: A count, without quotes; or a limit or range on one; or a formula. In a field that gives the most or the least, a bare number is that limit.

printed unit.means: A number in a unit that is kept as printed.

examples: Off the carpet on the bar.

texts.means: Words, or a list of them.

says.means: Words in which {height} stands for this record's value and {bale.mass} for another's. A limit prints without its words, so write "at most {limits.height.max}". A number that a field holds is named, not typed.
examples: At most {limits.reach.far} out, in the last {endgame.last}.

src.means: Where it is written, or a list. The first word is an ID in `sources`. An ID alone is enough when the source has no sections.

date.means: A date, as year, month and day.

differs.means: A list of what other sources say.

examples.says: The text calls it a square.

was.means: A list of what it was before.

word.means: One of a list of words.

words.means: Some of a list of words, or one.

outline.means: A list of points in the field's frame; or a rectangle, hexagon or circle with its middle at `at`, turned by `faces`. Inside a shape, points are from `at`, along `faces`.

shape.means: A shape is drawn around its record's `at`, turned by `faces`, and stands on the height in `at`: that is the height of its lowest point, so a ball at 0 in rests on the carpet. Points of an outline inside a shape are from `at`, along `faces`. If no source gives the height a solid starts at, leave it out of `at` and put that in `unknown`.

shapes.means: A list of shapes, each with its own `at`, which is from the record's and stands the same way. A part's `at` is turned by the record's `faces`; a part has no `faces` of its own.

height.means: A height from the carpet, or `none` for no limit.

spots.means: Names and where each is; or a row; or a ring.

first spot.means: One spot, or several named ones.

starts.means: What is there at the start, by piece. A count belongs to the record of one alliance, all its spots together; for one spot, write {"each": "spot", "is": 1}. Do not type a count that the spots already make. `left over` is the total less everything that other places start with.

hold limit.means: A number for each piece, or one number.

cap.means: The most, for each alliance in a match: a number; or a number for each `spot`, `alliance` or ID, with `when` if it is only at some times.

circuits.means: A number, `any` for no limit, or an object that says what is counted.

on.means: For each kind of device, how many of this load one device may run. A kind that is left out may not run it; `any` is no limit.

timer.means: From and to, as the match timer counts down.

variants.means: Each kind of variant, and its names. The first is used when a question names none.

when.means: A list of periods, windows, states and variants that must all be true. `not` may go in front, and `my` or `their` in front of a state; a state with no such word is mine. An empty list is always.

list of whens.means: A list of `when` lists, and any one is enough.

conditions.means: [who, how, what], which reads as English. Only the listed words are used. How is one of `measures` or `compares`. Who is `my`, `their` or `either` and then robot, bumpers, person, alliance or an ID from `counts`; or `the piece`, or `the` and a piece's ID. What is `my`, `their` or `any` and then an ID; `carpet`; a number, formula or value by variant; `every robot`; or a list, which may hold words for a part that has no ID. A list of conditions that must all be true. {"any": [...]} needs one, and {"all": [...], "when": [...]} groups some at a time.

must not.means: true, or the conditions that make it wrong.

pieces.means: A piece's ID, or a list.

things.means: An ID, with `my`, `their` or `any` in front if each alliance has one and bare if not; or a list of them.

things touched.means: `their robot`, or IDs with `my`, `their` or `any` in front; or a list.

touchable.means: A list of IDs with `my`, `their` or `any` in front, or bare if it belongs to neither alliance, or words for a part that has no ID.

goes to.means: The ID of a place or a zone, or `out` when it leaves play. A piece that falls on the floor goes to the zone where it falls.

after period.means: A time after a period's end. The field's name is `after_` and the period's ID.

people.means: Each kind of person, by ID, and `together` for limits on several kinds at once.

several people.means: A list of kinds of people.

who.means: A list of `robot`, people from game.json, or `anyone`.

loads.means: A list of the IDs of loads in `parts`.

longer than.means: A term that has a time, or a time.

cost.means: A list, and all of it adds up. Each is a foul ID or an object.

records.means: Records of a kind, by ID.

list of.means: A list of things of a kind.

tags.means: What all the tags share, and each tag by ID.

limits.means: The limits that a season has, by the names in `limits`.

parts.means: Groups of records. A group may have `about`.

game.means: Edition, sources, what changes a number (`variants`), where positions are measured from, people. Everyone needs it.

edition.means: Which edition of the manual this folder holds, and its date.

sources.means: Every document that a value comes from, by a short ID. The first word of each `src` is one of these IDs.

variants.means: The kinds of field, event and match, and anything that a team chooses, such as a gate's height: what a value may depend on (`by`). A question that names none gets the first of each.

frame.means: Where positions are measured from, and which way each axis goes.

people.means: Each kind of person on a team's side, by ID. `together` limits several kinds at once.

accuracy.means: How near the real field is to the numbers.

clock.means: Periods, windows (spans of time with a name), states (things that are true for a while). For strategy, rehearsal and controls.

periods.means: The parts of a match, in order.

windows.means: Spans of time with a name. Windows may overlap.

states.means: Things that are true for a while.

field.means: Size, zones, lines, solids, ways through, things robots hang on, vision tags. For every design phase and vision.

symmetry.means: How red's side is made from blue's, unless a record has its own.

guardrail.means: The wall along the long sides of the field.

zones.means: Areas of the field that rules or scores name.

lines.means: Lines of the field that rules or scores name.

solids.means: Things that a robot can run into.

passages.means: Ways through, over or under something.

equipment.means: Lights, station shelves, buttons and the like.

tags.means: The vision tags, by ID, and what they all share.

pieces.means: Each piece: shape, size, mass. For every design phase.

places.means: Everywhere a piece can be: where it starts, comes from, can be put, and goes next. For strategy, rehearsal and concepts.

scoring.means: What earns points, what is counted, what fouls cost. For strategy, rehearsal and concepts.

total.means: How many of each piece there are in all, by piece.

awards.means: Everything that earns points or ranking points.

judged.means: How long after a period an award is still looked at. A piece counted then belongs to the period that ended.

fouls.means: What a broken rule may cost: fouls and cards.

conduct.means: What robots and people may not do, and what it costs. For strategy, rehearsal and controls. Keyed by rule code, or by an ID when the manual gives no code (setup, cards, the order of placing robots).

robot.means: What a robot must be. For every design phase and inspection.

limits.means: The numbers that a robot must keep to. The names are the same every season, and no other names are allowed. A season with no such rule leaves the name out, and a program reads that as no limit. Each also has `says` where the measuring needs it.

parts.means: Groups of records: what may be used, and how it is wired. An ID is used once in a group.

rules.means: A record for every construction and inspection rule, keyed by code, each with its own `says`. Numbers come from `limits`, `parts` or the record's own fields.

terms.means: The manual's defined words. Everyone needs it. A word that is already the ID of something else (a zone, a piece) has no term: its `says` is there.

roots.means: Words that begin a path in place of an ID: size: The field's size. limits: The robot's limits. tags: The vision tags. total: How many of each piece there are. judged: How long after a period awards count. parts: What may be used. guardrail: The wall along the long sides. accuracy: How near the real field is to the numbers.

says.means: The whole meaning in our own words. Numbers come from the fields: {height} is this record's, {bale.mass} another's. A limit prints without its words: {limits.height.max} prints 4 ft, so write "at most {limits.height.max}".

code.means: The manual's rule code, or a list. Codes change each season, so programs never use them.

src.means: Where it is written: "manual 3.2", or a list. The first word is an ID in `sources`.

unknown.means: A list: what a reader would look for and no source gives. A known fact never goes here.

differs.means: Other sources that say something different. On a whole record each holds `says`.

was.means: Earlier values or wording, on a record or on one value.

of.means: What is measured, from where to where, when the name does not say.

placed.means: What any record that stands somewhere may have.

alliance.means: `each`: blue and red each have one. Write blue's; red's is made by the symmetry. Left out, there is one and it belongs to neither.

symmetry.means: This record's own symmetry, if it is not the field's.

at.means: Where it is: [x, y] or [x, y, z] in the field's frame. A solid stands on z: it is the height of its lowest point.

faces.means: Which way it looks in plan: 0 deg is +X, 90 deg is +Y, anticlockwise from above. Shapes and outlines are turned by it. 0 deg if left out.

spots.means: Several of the same thing: where each is.

no_geometry.means: Why it has no position or shape, in words: no source gives it, or it needs none. `rules check` lists it. A zone, line, solid or hang that a rule or a score names must have an outline, `from` and `to`, a shape, an `at` or `spots`, or this. `unknown` is for anything else that no source gives.

value.means: A value that needs more than its printed form.

of.means: What is measured, from where to where, when the name does not say.

src.means: The source of this value, when it is not the record's.

assumed.means: Why this value was chosen, when no source prints it.

differs.means: What other sources say instead. `is` is the one to use.

each.means: What it is counted for each of: `spot`, `alliance` or an ID.

is.means: The value that the other source gives.

says.means: What the other source says, in our own words.

until.means: The date on which it stopped being so, as 2031-02-04.

says.means: What was said until then, in our own words.

frame.means: The field's frame: every position is measured in it.

accuracy.means: How near the real field is to the numbers.

decimal.means: The drawings' tolerance on a length.

angle.means: The drawings' tolerance on an angle.

most.means: The most of them that a team may have.

together.means: A limit on several kinds of people together.

control.means: Who controls the robots in it, in words, such as `none` or `drivers`.

window.means: A span of time with a name, inside one period. It has one of `first`, `last` and `timer`.

in.means: The period that it is in.

first.means: It is the first so much of the period.

last.means: It is the last so much of the period.

timer.means: From and to, as the match timer counts down in that period: ["1:15", "0:50"].

state.means: Something that is true for a while.

starts.means: What makes it start, in words.

needs.means: Conditions that must be true for it to start.

or_until.means: What ends it sooner, in words.

grace.means: Time added after it ends. The state is over, but what `of` or `says` names still counts.

true.means: When it is true: a list of `when` lists, and any one is enough.

length.means: Along x, between the faces that look into the field and bound it.

width.means: Along y, between the faces that look into the field and bound it.

surface.means: What the floor is, in words.

guardrail.means: The wall along the long sides of the field.

gates.means: How many gates it has in all.

edge.means: Whether the tape is part of it. Left out, it is not said.

height.means: How high it reaches from the carpet, or `none` for no limit. Left out, no source gives it.

wide.means: A printed width. `of` says which way.

deep.means: A printed depth. `of` says which way.

from_wall.means: A printed distance from the alliance wall.

solid.means: Something that a robot can run into.

wide.means: A printed width. `of` says which way.

tall.means: A printed height from its foot to its top.

passage.means: A way through, over or under something. `at` is its middle, and `faces` the direction through it.

height.means: Carpet to the lowest thing overhead.

rise.means: How high a robot climbs to go over.

slope.means: How steep the way over is, from level.

equipment.means: A light, shelf, button or the like.

hang.means: Something that robots hang on. `at` is the middle of a bar, the lowest point of a chain, the middle of the bottom of a frame or post.

diameter.means: How thick the bar, chain or post is.

width.means: How wide it is, end to end.

may_touch.means: What a hanging robot may also touch: IDs, or words for a part that has none.

may_not_touch.means: What a hanging robot may not touch: IDs, or words for a part that has none.

black.means: The side of the black square.

panel.means: The side of the panel that the tag is on.

measured.means: What point of a tag the positions are measured to, in words.

at.means: Where its point is (`measured` says which point).

faces.means: Which way it looks in plan.

tilt.means: How far it leans from upright so that it looks downward.

panel.means: Its own panel, when it is not like the others.

spot.means: One of several of the same thing.

faces.means: Which way it looks in plan.

row.means: Spots in a straight row, numbered from 1 or named by `names`.

first.means: The first spot. It may hold several named spots, which makes 1.a, 1.b, 2.a and so on.

names.means: Names to use in place of numbers.

ring.means: Spots around a point, numbered from 1 or named by `names`. A ring turns each spot's `faces` too.

step.means: The angle from each to the next, anticlockwise from above.

first.means: The first spot. It may hold several named spots, which makes 1.a, 1.b, 2.a and so on.

names.means: Names to use in place of numbers.

stiff.means: Whether it keeps its shape when pressed.

still_one_if.means: What a worn or damaged one must still be like to count, in words.

made_of.means: What it is made of, in words.

place.means: Somewhere that a piece can be. `at` is the middle of an opening or a surface, the tip of a post, or the middle of where pieces rest.

starts.means: What is there at the start: {"bale": 17}, or {"bale": "left over"} for what the other places do not use.

holds.means: The most it can hold, by piece.

opening.means: A hole that pieces go through.

post.means: A rod that goes through a piece.

slide.means: The slope of a slide behind an opening that people feed pieces down.

takes.means: Who can put what here, and what it earns.

gives.means: What comes out, and to where.

then.means: Where a piece goes once taken.

opening.means: A hole that pieces go through.

outline.means: Its shape: a circle, a rectangle [width, height] or a hexagon.

slope.means: How the opening's plane stands: 0 deg is flat, 90 deg is upright. In between, it looks upward, toward `faces`.

from.means: The side that pieces come from.

lip.means: How far its edge sticks up or out.

post.means: A rod that goes through a piece.

slope.means: How the rod stands from level: 90 deg is upright. In between, it rises toward `faces`.

size.means: Its size: two lengths, along `faces` and across.

slope.means: How it leans: 0 deg is flat.

counts.means: What must be true for it to count, in words.

give.means: What comes out, and to where.

to.means: Where it goes: the place's own alliance's, if that place is for each.

then.means: Where a piece goes once taken.

to.means: Where: an ID, or `out` when it leaves play.

of.means: Whose: `mine` or `theirs`, as the place's own alliance sees it.

total.means: How many of each piece there are in all.

count.means: Something that a condition counts. It `adds` the points of awards, `counts` how often awards are earned, takes the `smallest_of` or `third_largest_of` the pieces in some places, or `says` it.

of.means: Who it is counted for, in words: usually `alliance`.

adds.means: The awards whose points are added up.

counts.means: The awards whose times earned are counted.

when.means: Only what is earned then counts.

smallest_of.means: The places: it is the fewest pieces in any of them.

third_largest_of.means: The places: it is the third largest number of pieces in any of them.

award.means: Something that earns points or ranking points.

per.means: What it is earned once for each of, in words: `piece`, `robot` or `match`.

points.means: The points, by when. Of the rows that are true, the one with the most entries in `when` counts (`not lit` is one); two that tie are refused.

looked_at.means: When a program looks whether its `needs` are true. Every award per robot has it.

easier.means: The `needs` that are enough at its `when`.

most.means: A cap on how many are earned.

points.means: Points for an award at some time.

needs.means: The conditions that are enough then.

judged.means: How long after a period some awards are still looked at. A field named `after_` and a period's ID, such as `after_auto`, holds the time for that period.

or_sooner.means: What ends the looking sooner, in words.

after_.means: `after_` and a period's ID: how long after that period they are still looked at.

foul.means: What a broken rule may cost.

points_to_them.means: The points that the other alliance gets.

conduct.means: What robots and people may not do. Every rule has `says` and `cost`. A rule that a program computes from has an `act` as well, with `must_not`, `only_if` or `limit`. `who` and `when` may be on any rule.

act.means: What kind of act it is about.

what.means: What is touched: `their robot`, or IDs.

through_pieces.means: `true`: contact through a piece counts too.

whoever_starts.means: `true`: it does not matter who starts the contact.

into.means: Only launches into this are judged by the rule. Left out, every launch is.

limit.means: How many: a number for each piece (`hold`), or a number of robots of one alliance (`cross`).

longer_than.means: How long it must last to count: a term or a time.

where.means: Where it is about, if it is about keeping pieces somewhere.

who.means: Who must obey: `robot` if left out, or a list of `robot`, people from game.json, or `anyone`.

must_not.means: `true`, or the conditions that make it wrong.

only_if.means: The conditions that make it right.

cost.means: What it costs. A rule that costs nothing has an empty list.

longest.means: The longest that it may go on, such as one robot keeping another from moving.

apart.means: How far apart the robots must be for it to end.

cost.means: One thing that a broken rule costs: a foul ID, or an object with one of `foul`, `award`, `deny`, `either` and `words`. A rule's `cost` is a list, and all of it adds up.

to.means: Who the award is given to, in words.

either.means: Fouls, one of which is given.

words.means: What happens, when it is none of the others.

again.means: Only when it happens again in the same match, phase or event.

instead_of.means: A foul in this list that is then not given.

each.means: Once for each of this, in words.

every.means: One for each such time that passes while it goes on, and none at the start. For one at once and more as it goes on, the list has both: ["minor", {"foul": "minor", "every": "3 s"}].

against.means: Who it counts against, if it is not the one that broke the rule.

next_match.means: `true`: it is given in the next match.

max.means: The most that it may weigh.

without.means: What is left off the scale.

about.means: What is true of a whole group of parts.

allow.means: Whether anything else may be used. With no `about`, it is not said.

part.means: Something that may be used, or a row of a wiring table.

kind.means: For a device that runs others: what kind of device.

only_for.means: A list of loads: the device may run these and no others, whatever its `kind` allows. A load is a record with `on`, named by its ID.

on.means: For a motor or other load: how many one device of each kind may run. A kind that is left out may not run it. `any` is no limit, and {"is": 1, "of": "each channel"} is per channel. With no `on` at all, nothing is said of what runs it.

protection.means: The breaker or fuse of a circuit.

each.means: How many circuits the breaker or fuse may feed: a number, `any`, or an object.

thinnest.means: The thinnest wire. A thicker wire has a smaller AWG.

for.means: What a row is about, in words.

rule.means: A construction or inspection rule, keyed by its code.

term.means: A word that the manual defines.

lasts.means: How long, when the word is about a time.

extra.means: A value that is not named here.

padding.means: The padding. Its sizes are extra values.

backing.means: What the padding is backed by.

numbers.means: The team numbers on the bumpers.

stroke.means: How thick the lines of the digits are.

perimeter.means: The outline of the robot without bumpers.

size.means: The length of a string pulled around it.

bump.means: How far a bolt head may stick out of it.

start.means: How a robot stands when the match starts.

where.means: Conditions that are true when the match starts.

overhang.means: What may reach beyond the perimeter, in words.

height.means: How tall a robot may be.

max.means: The tallest it may ever be.

reach.means: How far a robot may reach out.

sides.means: On how many sides at once.

weight.means: What a robot may weigh: named limits, each with `max` and `without`.

inspected.means: All that is brought to inspection.

hold.means: The most pieces that a robot may have at once, by piece.

preload.means: The most pieces that a robot may start with, by piece.

low.means: The bottom of the bumper zone, from the floor.

high.means: The top of the bumper zone, from the floor.

hard.means: How far hard parts may be from the perimeter.

corner.means: The padding at a corner: how far out from the corner it must be, or words.

tolerance.means: What is allowed on each size at inspection.

backing.means: What the padding is backed by.

numbers.means: The team numbers on the bumpers.

cover.means: What covers the padding, in words.

drive.means: What drives the robot over the floor.

motors.means: How many motors may drive it.

part.means: The most that one part may cost.

console.means: The operator's console: its own numbers.

rate.means: The most data in a second.

axis.means: Which way it lies; x if left out.

ring.means: A ring that lies flat, round in section. Its `thick` is (`outside` - `inside`) / 2.

thick.means: How thick the ring itself is.

axis.means: Which way it lies; x if left out.

join.means: A list of shapes that make one, each with its own `at`, from the record's, and standing the same way.

cut.means: A list of shapes: the first, with the others cut out of it, each with its own `at`, from the record's, and standing the same way.

points.means: One direction that a point looks, from `faces`.

alliance.means: Whether blue and red each have one.

each.means: Blue and red each have one.

symmetry.means: How red's copy is made from blue's, for a field length x width.

mirror.means: Point (x, y) becomes (length - x, y), and direction a becomes 180 - a. It also swaps left and right in an outline, an opening or a shape that is not the same on both sides.

turn.means: Point (x, y) becomes (length - x, width - y), and direction a becomes a + 180.

state_of.means: What a state is true of.

match.means: There is one for the whole match.

edge.means: Whether a zone's tape is part of it.

tape inside.means: The tape is part of the zone.

tape outside.means: The tape is not part of the zone.

height.means: A zone's height, when it is not a quantity.

for.means: Who a zone or line is for.

under.means: Below something; its `height` is the room.

hang_kind.means: The kinds of thing that robots hang on, and what `at` is for each.

bar.means: A straight bar; `at` is its middle.

chain.means: A chain; `at` is its lowest point.

frame.means: A frame; `at` is the middle of its bottom.

post.means: A post; `at` is the middle of its bottom.

ledge.means: An edge to rest or hang on; `at` is its middle.

starts.means: What a place starts with, when it is not a number.

left over.means: The total, less everything that other places start with. With `alliance: each`, half of it for each alliance. Only one place may start with what is left over of a piece.

opening_from.means: The side that pieces come to an opening from.

takes_by.means: Who puts a piece in a place.

takes_how.means: How a piece must end up.

field.means: The field itself: the piece is picked up, or comes out by itself.

gives_to.means: Where a given piece goes, when it is not an ID.

whose.means: Whose place a piece goes to.

mine.means: Of the alliance whose place this is.

theirs.means: Of the other alliance than the one whose place this is.

goes_to.means: Where a piece goes once taken, when it is not an ID.

act.means: The kinds of act that a program can judge, and the fields that each uses, besides `must_not`, `only_if`, `when` and `unless`.

touch.means: Contact that depends on a zone, a time or a thing. Uses `what`, `through_pieces`, `whoever_starts`.

launch.means: Where a piece may be launched or put by a robot. Uses `piece`, `into`. A rule about throwing only is words.

hold.means: How many pieces. Uses `limit` (a number for each piece), `longer_than`, `where`.

cross.means: Where a robot may be, or how many robots. With `limit`, at most that many robots of one alliance may meet `must_not` at once.

feed.means: How pieces may enter or be kept. Uses `piece`, `who`.

looked_at.means: When an award's `needs` are looked at.

any time.means: At any time in the period: once is enough.

at the end.means: When the period in `when` ends, with `judged`.

again.means: Within what a rule must be broken again.

phase.means: In the same part of an event, such as its qualification matches.

examples.means: These are examples; others may be used.

device.means: The kinds of device that run others.

own.means: A controller built into one motor.

axis.means: Which way a cylinder or tube lies.

who.means: Who must obey a rule, besides the people of game.json.

anyone.means: Whoever does it: the rule names nobody.

touched.means: What is touched, when it is not an ID.

their robot.means: A robot of the other alliance.

sides.means: Whose, at the front of who a condition is about. `my` and `their` are always seen from the robot that acts.

my.means: Of the one that acts. `my` and `their` are always seen from the robot that acts, so they never change color.

either.means: True if it is true of mine or of theirs.

someone.means: Who a condition is about, after the side, besides an ID from `counts`.

robot.means: The robot, bumpers and all. `their robot` is the one touched in a `touch` rule, and any opponent elsewhere.

alliance.means: The alliance. Only a state, a count or a `to` is of a whole alliance.

the.means: At the front of a piece that a condition is about.
Before `piece` or a piece's ID: the piece that the rule is about.

the_piece.means: The piece that the rule is about.

owners.means: Whose thing, at the front of an ID.

any.means: Either's, or one that belongs to neither.

all.means: All of these, at the times in `when` if it is given.

what.means: What a condition compares with, besides an ID, a number, a formula or a list.

every robot.means: As many as the alliance has in the match.

measures.means: How something stands to a zone, a line or a thing.

partly in.means: Any part is in, in plan and below the zone's `height`; and so also when all of it is.

beyond.means: Completely past it, on the side away from the robot's own wall.

over.means: Any part is over it, in plan.

above.means: All of it is higher than all of that thing.

touching.means: Touches it; of a list, any one of them.

not touching.means: Does not touch it; of a list, none of them.

touching only.means: Touches nothing but these. It need not touch any of them.

compares.means: How a count stands to a number.

my.means: Mine. A state with no word in front is mine, if it is of an alliance; of a robot, piece or place, the one that is judged; of the match, the same for both.

limit.means: The words in front of a number that make it a limit.

sin.means: Sine of an angle, which needs no conversion.

atan2.means: The angle whose tangent is the first over the second.
